newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom predicts mobile phone boom.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom predicts mobile phone boom.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom MobilNet GmbH (T-Mobil), a subsidiary of Deutsche Telekom AG, said on Monday it expects the number of people using mobile phones in Germany to triple to around 15 million by the year 2000.

T-Mobil managing director Lothar Hunsel told reporters that the company had raised its previous growth forecasts to 15 million at the end of the century. Earlier forecasts predicted growth of between 10 million and 15 million users.
There are currently some five million mobile phone connections in Germany. T-Mobil is Germany's largest provider of mobile communications services.

It operates the D1 digital cellular network, which has around two million connections, the C-net analogue network, with some 600,000 connections, and has around one million paging service connections.

Its competitors in Germany are Mannesmann Mobilfunk, which operates the D2 digital cellular network and has over two million connections, and E-Plus, the mobile phone venture led by Veba AG and Thyssen AG.
T-Mobil was gaining 60,000 to 80,000 new connections per month, Hunsel said. He did not say whether this referred to net or gross connections.
